name: CatalogueViewToggle
intent: Persisted table-or-cards switch for a catalogue page, plus the responsive grid its cards land in.
when: A list page offers both a dense table and a card grid over the same rows
The choice should survive a reload
whenNot: Choosing a value rather than a presentation -> use ToggleGroup directly
Only one presentation exists -> render DataTable alone

chooseOver.because: Four catalogue pages each re-typed the toggle, its icons, the de-select swallow and the grid tracks; this keeps them identical and keeps the mode reaching DataTable through only showColumnToggle and renderGrid, so the table is never unmounted and never loses its sort, page index or column visibility.

lineage.authoredBy: Extracted from the four catalogue pages found in the missing-widgets template review (2026-08-25)

extracted: segmented toggle with its de-select swallow

lineage.supersedes: The page-local view toggles in wc3-process-list-view, wc3-pipeline-list-view, wc3-product-catalogue-view and wc3-analysis-saved-view
notes: Component tier, not widget: a presentation switch carries no domain meaning and no data contract.
Deliberately does NOT wrap DataTable — doing so would fight the one-table-mounted-for-life invariant those pages protect.

props.name: tableLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the table option. Defaults to "Table view".

props.name: cardsLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the cards option. Defaults to "Card view".

props.name: ...props
props.description: All standard HTML attributes are supported.

usage: Use CatalogueViewToggle when you need to collect user input or allow users to make selections. This component provides a consistent interaction pattern that users will find familiar and accessible.

CatalogueViewToggle should be used within forms or interactive interfaces where user data collection is required. Ensure proper labeling and validation feedback for accessibility. Avoid using this component for read-only or display-only content.

anatomy.description: CatalogueViewToggle is composed of the following parts:

bestPractices.title: Use semantic props
bestPractices.description: Use the component's built-in props rather than className overrides.

bestPractices.title: Don't override core styles
bestPractices.description: Avoid using className to override the component's fundamental styling.

bestPractices.title: Provide accessible labels
bestPractices.description: Include proper ARIA labels for screen reader users.

bestPractices.title: Don't skip accessibility
bestPractices.description: Never omit accessibility attributes for interactive components.

bestPractices.title: Handle all states
bestPractices.description: Account for loading, error, empty, and success states.

bestPractices.title: Don't ignore edge cases
bestPractices.description: Avoid showing broken UI when data is missing or loading.
